title: Working source actions do not yet mean reliable write-task completion
text: All four methods scored 0/4 on the new write variants. The SDK passed its two read-control episodes. This is a 24-episode training pilot, not evidence about all AppWorld tasks.

title: One SDK failure made exactly the requested changes
text: afc0fce_1__sdk__0 passed all eight world-state checks but submitted an unnecessary count. The shared prompt already told every method to omit an answer when none is required. Use the “Correct writes, failed answer” filter; the official score remains a failure.

title: Another SDK episode mutated the wrong contact group
text: afc0fce_2__sdk__0 correctly traversed incoming transactions and called the actions, but omitted the sender-group constraint. Its raw TS counterpart also omitted that filter and initially acted on only one API page. More capable execution can still produce incorrect changes.

title: REPL recovery still consumes the small turn budget
text: Both second-repeat SDK write episodes exhausted 14 turns without a mutation. Repeated top-level declarations and confusion between an awaited query page and an iterable query handle consumed turns. Do not attribute these failures to the source-write bridge.

title: Main realm fix verified without a wrapper
text: Main 5a0af21 is merged and rebuilt. The real consumer accepts REPL-created action inputs; no input-cloning adapter was added. Real AppWorld smoke tests verify read-after-write and successful same-key replay without duplicate comments.

title: Keep the next experiment narrow
text: Keep all four methods and this task subset. Test budget sensitivity separately from a clearer write-only completion example. Then examine selection-before-mutation guidance and source-error handling before adding another domain. No flat-array condition is required.

title: Cost and timing are recorded, including failures
text: The 24 episodes total 8.7 minutes of recorded episode time and $0.1574 estimated model cost. Per-turn input/output tokens, model time, execution time, errors, API requests and evaluator results are available in the explorer.
